Hi Ivan. I can do so. More than likely the internal HDD is messed up, hardware wise.

Your suggestion of an SSD is actually a great one. The amount of RAM inside the laptop is good.

Sometimes errors on the HDD can be repaired by Windows. But an old laptop HDD? Those suffer hardware damage and that is unrepairable.

So it is highly likely that the HDD needs replacement anyway. 

A replacement HDD will cost at least 200.000Gs in CDE and that is without what i charge. 

So, is that old laptop still worth the costs that your friend is willing to make? 

It might be, if the laptop was treated with silk gloves all those years. But if it isn't, there will soon be other problems coming. Screen, for example. Or networking hardware runs out of support. Which cripples any Windows installation nowadays. Happened to my old little laptop. Now it runs Linux.


If the laptop has not been treated so well, your friend should spend more and get a new laptop, he will be better off in the long run.

Besides, his current laptop will be obsolete in 2025. Because then all support for Windows 10 is stopped by MS and everyone has to run Windows 11. Which comes with serious changes to system requirements.

Heck, at least half of the desktops at WPG are not allowed to run Windows 11. By decree of MS. 

Better ask your friend what is the maximum he wants to spend on his old laptop. With replacement parts included it will already be 400.000Gs. 

And sorry to say, but old laptops like his are hardly worth spending that money on.

Old laptops like his may have a large screen, but more often than not a very crappy resolution.

The HP brand is not known for putting good monitors with large resolution in their laptops.

Getting a domain, well, you will require a good name. And as it is a 'play-server, you probably don't give a crap about the TLD.

TLD's like '.com' or '.ai' or '.py' are not cheap. Not anymore at least.

As you own the VPS I would suggest that you think of the domain name and register it via CloudFlare too.

https://www.cloudflare.com/products/registrar/

As example, a link to an  overview of yearly prices for domain name 'openklauw' with different TLD's:
https://domains.cloudflare.com/?domain=openklauw

I tend to focus on the renewal price more than on the initial price. Some can be quite deceptive.
Not CloudFlare's fault, any TLD is managed by the country that owns that specific TLD. '.py' is from Paraguay and Paraguay decides the renewal costs.

Also, I look at the TLD itself. Can I use it in the domain name?
Can I make it funny (to me)? Funny tends to memorable.
Can I expect (legal) problems with a certain TLD? Better safe than sorry and select another one.

Some spitballing about choice of domain name:

OpenClaw > OpenKlauw (in Dutch) > Hand (in Dutch) is associated with 'klauw' > The word 'klauwen' is associated with stealing > stealing is associated with untrustworthy people > OpenClaw is not the most trustworthy AI project out there > so, perhaps a good domain name could be '5fingerdiscount' for this play project?

Sometime during installation you should have gotten the 'OpenClaw Gateway Token'. This is an essential token. Taken from their website:
Source of truth: the Gateway
OpenClaw is designed around a single Gateway process that owns session state.
UIs (macOS app, web Control UI, TUI) should query the Gateway for session lists and token counts.
In remote mode, session files are on the remote host; “checking your local Mac files” won’t reflect what the Gateway is using.
https://docs.openclaw.ai/reference/session-management-compaction#source-of-truth-the-gateway
You may need to look in files (located where erebus is installed) to check if your installation received such a token.
